editorialTake:
Luxury and jewellery brands are about to face a new kind of digital arms race: the value of proprietary data and customer touchpoints is rising fast, and those who rely on public data or generic AI tools will fall behind. Amazon’s launch of Alexa for Shopping, after scrapping its earlier Rufus chatbot, shows how the biggest players are doubling down on AI assistants that sit directly between the brand and the consumer. Meanwhile, Wirestock’s $23 million raise to supply exclusive creative datasets to AI labs signals a shift: open web data is no longer enough to train the next generation of AI, and those with unique assets, visual, experiential, or customer, suddenly have leverage.

On the operational side, Marks & Spencer’s £67.5 million investment in an automated distribution hub is another sign that the winners will be those who control their own tech stack and data flows, not those who outsource or depend on third parties. Even Anthropic, whose CFO says 90% of their code is now AI-generated, is only able to move this quickly because they own both the tools and the data. For luxury and jewellery, where every touchpoint and every image is brand-defining, the risk is clear: let others mediate your data, and you lose the edge.

Some will argue that luxury is immune, that the emotional and tactile nature of jewellery and high fashion can’t be replaced by algorithms. That’s only true if you keep control of the digital layer, your customer data, your content, your online experience. If you hand that over to a marketplace, a generic AI, or a third-party logistics provider, you’re handing over your future differentiation.

In the next quarter, I would push every luxury and jewellery operator to audit where their customer data and creative assets actually live, and who else can access or use them. Start building your own private datasets and AI tools, even if only for internal use. The brands that treat proprietary data as a strategic asset will be the ones whose stories and experiences still matter when the next wave of AI hits retail.
oneSentenceSummary: AI labs’ urgent investments in proprietary multimodal datasets suggest that publicly available web data is rapidly losing strategic value for next-generation model training.
